patrick-w-atwater.text: Atwater's campaign lists three priorities: coordinate more with first responders and speed Altadena's fire recovery; "invest in innovative local water supplies like water recycling and stormwater recharge to save ratepayer money"; and stop "buck passing" between agencies.

patrick-w-atwater.text: "It makes less than zero sense to let rainwater flow into the ocean while importing expensive and environmentally more impactful water from the Colorado river and Sierra Nevada snowpack — even less sense given the realities of boom and bust precipitation patterns with climate change."

patrick-w-atwater.text: Calls LADWP's Pueblo water right claims "unethical, uneconomical and unsustainable," saying LA imports water that drains Mono Lake "while blocking stormwater recharge projects in the LA basin."

source.title: Future of the Foothills — Patrick Atwater for FMWD campaign page

patrick-w-atwater.text: Proposes a "master protocol for climate adaption" assessing flood, fire, wind and earthquake vulnerabilities and investing iteratively in "no to low regrets solutions."

patrick-w-atwater.text: In an August 2026 op-ed written as a candidate, Atwater said conservation alone "is not going to be enough" and urged "new, cost effective local water supplies," citing the CV Park stormwater project stalled by LADWP's water-rights stance.

patrick-w-atwater.text: In a July 2026 op-ed, urged replacing elementary schoolyard asphalt with permeable surfaces, bioswales and native plantings funded by Measure W, calling captured rain "a water supply investment as much as a parks investment."

patrick-w-atwater.text: In a January 2026 op-ed backing Glendale Community College's plan for a Montrose building, warned that "by resisting almost any change, we lose sight of how communities stay healthy," citing similar tensions over housing.
